[b] Some context and background about this game and why it's gonna get worse in 6 months from now around summer 2026 prepare for another storm of negative reviews: [/b] A while ago a publisher change happened so account migration was needed. Most players weren't informed and got their accounts forever lost. In a gacha game where most spent real money and time on it this is a huge issue. Now here we are in the present November 25th 2025 and the official WARP servers launched. Basically these servers make the game more of an mmorpg, however there is a catch that most players even myself aren't informed about. They will be seasonal content which means every 6 months the progression you made will be erased. I've played games like Path of Exile. Diablo, Black Desert that have seasonal content like leagues, expansions, seasonal servers however with these games since you are still playing the base game mostly with just some added mechanic and most a leaderboard to climb or with faster progression all your characters once seasonal content is done they migrate to the base game standard version or server whatever you wanna call it. The issue is that Tower of Fantasy is a gacha game, you use real money to pull for characters while in the WARP(mmorpg) servers they are just cosmetics think of characters like skins. So your progression once WARP season ends every 6 months will not migrate over to base standard server of Tower of Fantasy because it would be unfair to all the gacha players that spent money to pull for said characters. It baffles me why they would introduce a mechanic like this seasonal content wipe every 6 months if the base game doesn't support the characters migrating. The time you have to spend on a new character to get to endgame on this game and gear them up fully might take you months, meanwhile in Path of Exile as an example takes me 3 hours to complete story get to end game and 3-4 weeks to complete most challenges from the new league. Imagine replaying the same story and unlocking the same exploration content all the chests in the world every 6 months, spending months to upgrade your character and for all of it to just POOF! disappear once the season ends. This is the calm before the storm just like the publisher account migration debacle that got this game to a "Mixed" steam review score I predict that in Summer 2026 once all WARP accounts get wiped people will be pissed and this game will have "Very Negative" steam review score.

ToF Warp Server got the "idle game" treatment. There is auto battle, mandatory story skip, and your characters can loot the map for you so you don't have to explore. Now to level up and get rewards, you just have to farm bosses all day. The only good thing they did was remove the gacha part of the original game.

Would recommend if they removed 90% of the remaining story keeping players from the fun part. And seeing how they supposedly already removed a lot of story already I couldn't imagine what a slog the game was before. Combat is solid along with character customization, but the devs are hell bent on making sure you don't get to any of the fun. Because they believe their story is worth enduring as it vomits boring exposition at you trying to get you to care about flat characters with little to no facial animation and no time or anything eventful to make you care about the characters' drama and issues. This game will have you leave an area to only immediately tell you to run back down the same hallway for an overly long cutscene. To then tell you to run across the same hallway for another boring cutscene, then tell you to run down the same hallway again. Repeat for about 5-7 times then finally tell you to go kill something fun to repeat the cutscene cycle all over again. Yeah you can skip the cutscenes but not immediately all the time, as they hold you hostage for at least a minute before the option is available for "important parts". It sucks that western mmos look like crap and have combat to match, while eastern mmos have great combat and in the graphical style I prefer. But don't let you enjoy it without having to watch an entire season of their generic and lifeless anime to have one cool fight. If you want solid combat you can find it here, but keep in mind you will think about finding a sturdy tree branch or test the load bearing capability of your ceiling fan whenever you want to fight something new or make any progress.

I'm writing this review solely from my experience as a new Tower of Fantasy player on the Warp Server (the one where they removed the gacha and everyone can acquire everything for free). Turns out, removing the gacha doesn't fix a broken and flawed game. Everything about the movement, combat, sound effects, dodging, feels cheap. The combat doesn't feel impactful, all of the animations are very floaty, and dodging is very imprecise and laggy despite the game relying on perfect dodges. If you get hit at all, even by the smallest of enemies, you get interrupted, which makes the already janky dodging feel even worse. It's just not an enjoyable experience compared to other anime action RPGs have far more crisp and responsive combat systems. Meanwhile, audio sounds like it was recorded in a tin can with 0 bass, it's ear-grating and very low quality. Overworld movement is clunky and climbing frequently bugs out and causes my character to get stuck on a ledge. (I heard some of these things get better when you unlock later characters, but the process is timegated and will probably take ~1 month to unlock all of the characters with more modern updated designs. Until then, it appears I'm stuck using the cheap-feeling early designs from back when the game launched initially.) For the story, I can't even really review it because they for some reason got the GENIUS idea to force the player to skip most of Act 1 and go straight into Act 2 (and no, it's not a skip button, you literally are just going along with the story and then suddenly, they jump from early Act 1 into start of Act 2, skipping most of the Act 1 plot). Major plot points happen, a key character has a complete identity shift and makeover, another major character goes missing, and you see none of it. I can't be asked to care about the story when they literally force the player to skip it with a time skip that I didn't even know was going to happen. 0/10 story execution. Lastly, this is just your average mobile game slop UX. Nothing is clear, tons of red dots that eventually lead you to clicking on the cash shop, constant tutorial spam, dozens upon dozens of layered menus, it's a mess. If you want an anime action RPG, there's dozens of them out there now, gacha or non-gacha alike. There's just better stuff to spend your time on. My only positive takeaway from this game is that it visually looks quite nice and the character designs are flashy and attractive. That's about it.

The countless negative remarks are beyond frustrating. We live in an era of no one's ever happy it seems. I played Tower of Fantasy when it first came out and was pretty quickly pushed away because of it's gacha system. Underneath that I found a charming world that was fun to explore with funny tidbits and oddities here and there. I loved the character designs and really enjoyed the story. Sure it's quick, it's brief, but it's a mobile game and PC game. I'm not expecting Expedition 33 out of it. But as I said, that gacha just killed me, and it only got worse as time went on because of the array of things you had to pull for. Now? No gacha? I was wondering what the hook was? How do they monetize? I installed and got into it, I started over, despite having some good stuff who cares? It's free now right? Right! Immediately I was greeted with six weapons including one I wanted forever and couldn't get lucky enough to nab (much less get 7 of it to max in the original), and now it's just in my hands at the start. I was thrilled. Exploring about with some powerful weapons made it feel more casual but is that really a bad thing? I'm not looking for a time sink, I'm looking for something to goof around on with some friends when we're feeling a lull and this is perfect for it. And the monetization? You can buy the currency now, and it's got a few things as if you're impatient you can pull more weapons (You get a free one every day and can earn some more, you pull each day until you get them all) or there's cosmetics etc., there's also an auction house where players can sell things to earn some of the fancy currency. Or you can just earn the other currency as you meander about. I was confused as when you get to a certain point in the story it does jump you into the 2nd world. At first I was very confused and a bit put off, but, honestly? I never even knew there was other worlds until it did that. And oh my goodness the second world was gorgeous. Detail everywhere. I just got lost running around checking things out. Yes that did jumble the story for me but I'll survive. Even if you're just mildly curious, it's free, it's fun. If you like Breath of the Wild or Genshin Impact, you'll love this. Hell, even if you're excited about the prospect of Ananta? As I was exploring the 2nd world's city I found a movie theater, a bowling alley, an arcade, a pool, a park, a highway, and I explored maybe a tenth of the city. Guilds have their own amazing hangout spot that you can build up together too! It's a blast, but don't let my review or others decide for you; I urge you to come check it out yourself. So we are about to enter 4th week of the new MMO server release for this game and let's just say, if not for gacha removal, I wouldn't play it at all, but turns out, just gacha removal doesn't magically fix the game, as I spent time on this, I realized that issues that were present on original servers like technical issues and bugs, mobile UI with little adjustment for non mobile platforms as well low and in MMOs case, elitist playerbase that expects you to have max tier weapons and upgraded gear that only spenders or hardcore grinders can have on high tier raids that do not even presumably require it by displaying required combat power that you do have but they do not think its enough makes the whole experience quite...mix of good and bad, but mostly bad and that week is going to be final one that makes me want to not play again. But let's start with its story, the first element that it makes itself different from most usual gacha games - its on a darker side, which I would like if not for how...unstructured the whole story is, as first world's story is quite not only mediocre at best, but also disjointed by forced story skip, which makes the already unimpressive impression worse, but once you consider the latter areas, it becomes...mid? Well, not bad but not great which combined is not good because of bad earlier areas, and that's quite a bad thing. If only a better job was done overall to not feel bad about it. The gameplay - now that's actually a point I want to address, since gacha servers have a ongoing problem of years long powercreep where the new stuff is always better than old, meaning putting premium resources on old stuff would bite you back later, as well people using new stuff to one man instances meant for multiple people, a great way to make multiplayer an awful experience for people who wanted a fair game and not paid players showing their power over non payers. Even with free stuff the game throws at you, you will never compete with them as skill matters little to such people, only power. Of course i never played the gacha servers, but considering the experience I had in past games on mobile of similar caliber, well, that doesn't exactly give me good confidence on enjoying anything of that sort, even if its popular and good in people eyes because of design that throws that balance away. The MMO servers on other hand, instead suffer from fact you are expected to loot 24/7 if you want to get at the top, because if you dont, you wont catch up to top tier players and guilds, as many rewards and events are tied to activity, which also means the said guilds wont take you as they want the best of the best, this was not the case during the initial launch because...well, practically everyone is new, but despite not even a month in, the guilds pretty much started becoming elites for elites rather quickly. So unless you are capable of keeping up with them, consider yourself a loner, as amount of non elite but middle player guilds is rather...low, and if you are a casual, then consider yourself out, for even the gacha server with easier solo play still feels less balanced due to said powercreep. Now the weapons - they all play differently, some easier to use some harder, but considering in said gachas you swap characters with their weapons to do their thing, here you swap weapons instead, which is better and less confusing, but still feels weird compared to traditional games where you pick a class and pick a single weapon to use in combat, only swapping for specific needs, but oh well, another gacha inspiration - but on point for MMO server; you have 2 banners per season - one with earlier released weapons and another with newer, which due to fact the MMO server made them equal to each other in terms of relative power, means its more of pick your needed piece and upgrade it to your needs, but you can still feel the design difference between earlier and newer content, with newer stuff being much better in terms of quality, and in some, power. Its great they heavily rebalanced the weapons compared to gacha, but favorites in terms of strength still exist for some. The world - the enviroment, while solid, the quality is not good, and in certain areas you can see low quality textures on those, same goes for enemies who are not from newer areas or bosses, especially if they are speaking in cutscenes, their mouths do not move, and while worlds are solid, enviroment is not as good. But exploring the worlds is not boring at least, considering the inspiration material that is, with resources and loot to find, which you actually do need because you'll need all of it, and a lot for high tier upgrades. Characters - They have decent designs and solid voice acting from known actors, and they are either NPCs or linked to weapons(simulacrums), and the most notable thing about them is the fact you can use other weapons while using them, like a support using offensive weapons and vice versa, which is a feature that I do like as it makes them less bound to restrictions in terms of style, and allows for plenty of visual combinations for your liking. And with multiplayer this game focuses on, it makes it more impactful. Bugs - despite taking years of ongoing development, there's plenty, both minor and major ones, let's start with minor ones like being able to open electrified/burning chests of domain 9 that arent defused via statue upgrades if you are in climbing position, which also takes no animation to do so, to chests giving the message of not having enough keys to open as if they were supposed to be openable only via that when you dont have enough, getting stuck between certain objects and such, if you transmit while being engaged with enemies who knockback you, you'll teleport off area due to damage taken, certain story cutscenes being pre-rendered videos that have the male main character ignoring your cosmetics and current gender, characters who speak not always moving their mouths, to major ones like your character failing to teleport to group calls if they are moving fast enough, which results in team leaders kicking you out for failing to keep up, when really its the games fault for doing so, and others I possibly heard or seen but cannot explain. Despite the change to an MMO, it still has mobile game elements such as stamina, used for life class system, of 6 you can only take 2 to level up, and they all require stamina to progress and collect items, yet even in the first world you can encounter items that clearly are for later progression, as well sidequests which still rely on gacha server rules, like a quest to collect items that require stamina, and that's the least awful one, but the worst ones tend to be cooking quests that require level 15+ in the skill to progress, which in turn require like, level 70+ due to skills having a level requirement to advance and we cannot even reach said level at the moment of writing due to time gates of current season, because of the item in question being high level that is not the case in original, missing images when you get recipes from said quests because of course and training points from open world being useless to earn at the moment cause you cannot spend them in warp server. And then there's gold seller spammers in world chat, which even if you report them, another one takes their place, which means without active moderation, the game's not going to feel good, and while they generally appear during nighttime of server's region, they still show how bad the situation is. Due to word limit, I am concluding the review with a similar score it has on bilibili, which is an experience that has some good points, but hampered with aftermentioned bad things, which means unless you are a hardcore player willing to stomach bugs and design issues of not gacha/MMO limbo of a game, you'd have to avoid for the best. If it was not in either extremes of playerbase, I would have a better view of this.

I wish I could recommend ToF as it has some great gooner content and is the only legit action-MMO that uses a physics engine that I have personally played. Unfortunately it also has a lot of issues. About the new Warp servers: 1: The boob sliders and dormitory are removed. 2: It still has ridiculously expensive outfit gacha. 3: The mechanics around unlocking cosmetics are designed to milk hundreds, or even thousands, per outfit in a way that makes it impossible to know the price. As for the game itself, the list of issues is too long to name everything, but most of it stems from being a lazy port of a mobile game. Some of the issues that result from being a lazy port: While performing actions in the inventory or other menus the players character will move around and activate skills etc. that correspond to the buttons pressed. When there are popups or harvestable items on field the game will prioritize interacting with those items over combat actions. Meaning you may temporarily be unable to dodge or attack. Inputs for ranged weapons are wildly inconsistent and render at least half of the ranged weapons unusable on gamepad as a result. Bows and single shot ranged weapons perform well enough, fully automatic weapons require a press and hold that makes it impossible to simultaneously aim and fire a weapon. General issues: The game tends to crash in the Domain9 map, an issue that has been known and reported for years. Early into the game players are forced to skip the majority of the first chapter with a vague rundown of major events leaving players lost and confused if they had tried to follow it. This decision is a bit baffling as players have to go into story locked areas during later events. The lag is incredibly bad for an action game. My ping is typically 100+. This is aggravated by the games reliance on well timed dodging. To combat lag issues and mobile devices having the worst possible experience for any action game there is a heavy reliance on AOE spam. This results in the latest characters/weapons being very samey. For example, the newest ranged character plays no different from melee characters and cannot even aim manually like older ranged weapons. In the end it is all a bit frustrating as this game does one thing other "action-MMO's" don't, which is using a physics engine instead of dice rolls under the hood. Games like Tera or ESO try to create the illusion of being an action game while being standard tab-target MMO's in actuality. It really is a shame ToF doesn't have the necessary server performance or quality content to make use of this because it really is something unique and special in this genre.

Played at release, ~200 hours over a few months. But stopped playing bc of lack of polish. Imagine my surprise when they announced a soft reboot/global warp server, & none of these issues were fixed. This game died from a thousand papercuts when it first came out, & it’ll happen again. First, both systems are unoptimized. No dedicated keybinds for many of the buttons on pc, & all of the tutorials say “tap.” But the mobile port looks very bad. ENG voice acting is awful, and I heard it doesn’t improve. It’s clear the VAs aren’t shown what’s happening on screen. Sometimes delivery *is* good emotionally, but it doesn’t *match* what’s happening in the scene (most apparent with fight scenes). I don’t think they give the lines of the other char they’re supposed to be talking to, either, bc some back & forth dialogue just sounds super stiff/repetitive. One char is just text-to-speech. While I could tell ppl to use the CN/JP voice acting, the small text sometimes overlaps w/ each other so it’s unreadable, & gets cut off if it’s too long, so if you care about the story then ENG va is kinda required. Now I actually think the worldbuilding is strong compared to other gachas. But not how it’s presented, & that’s the snake eating its own tail. Bc the story is presented so poorly, ppl stopped caring about it, & bc existing players don’t care about the story anymore, Hotta doesn’t bother trying to make the story better. Thus, new players who actually DO care about story are turned off from the game. Rinse & repeat, & the story will never improve. Same thing with the ENG voice acting. Early character design was bad. It did that mecha sci-fi thing where chars just have mishmashed pieces of plastic on them & weird metal abs. Going from genshin—which basically *mastered* gacha char color palettes, accessories, & silhouette harmony—to ToF was painful. They’ve improved, but keep in mind that the early chars will be eyesores. There’s also legitimately zero dark-skinned chars. Even Genshin has a few. Char integration in the story is bad. Now that gacha is gone, maybe they’re trying to go for a Warframe-like story system, where side quests are where you learn about playable chars’ lore, & their involvement in the main story is kept to a minimum. This is fine, but it sticks out like a sore thumb for ToF’s genre (anime rpg). It’s just so hard to feel connected to any of the chars. Ex: the first playable char you meet in the main story (NOT counting Shirli bc she wasn’t playable at game release) was King, & his introduction doesn’t do him justice. He’s the announcer for a fight ring, & his only purpose is to explain the rules & who your opponents are. After this 1 minute of talking he never appears again. Instead of only making him the announcer, they should have also made him your final opponent, giving a story twist & making him look cooler. UI is still bad. You have to navigate through like three menus just to fish, the menu with all your options still looks bad even with the redesign. The buttons are in groups, except the group labels are tiny & tucked in all the way to the right of the menu. These labels don’t pop out & your eyes have to actively be searching for them. Settings is still disorganized & no borders/containers dividing each setting. After months I still didn’t understand how most of the menus worked/what they did. Maps for some areas are unreadable bc they don’t show elevation well. It’s worse when places overlap, so you end up tracking a quest & it’ll be miles above you with no obvious route to get to it. Map doesn’t show how things are connected elevation-wise, or where you can teleport to get to the place you wanna go to. Side modes are half-baked. There’s a housing & pet system, except you can’t customize the furniture in your house, nor can you interact with your pet beyond putting food in its bowl. It can’t follow you, can’t roam around the house, & will leave if you forget to feed it. Which, since you can’t do much with it, you will probably forget it exists. There’s also a “custom island” system in the gacha server, sort of like Genshin’s housing. Except once again, you can’t actually build any custom buildings/furniture. It’s more of a town idle game where you build a chosen set of uncustomizable shops in certain spots, & you can get resources from them at intervals. The warp server then removed this island gamemode. Sound design is fair except everything sounds slightly muffled/far away from the mic. Bc so many enemies have shields, you hear the same plastic-hitting sound for a while, getting bored. Relatedly, combat stales towards midgame, since so many enemies have shields & just tank your hits. Doing this over & over gets boring, & the visual effects/rewards weren’t enough to keep me hooked. There’s actually a fair amount of depth to combat; there’s a lot of combos each char can thread together. The issue is the content isn’t hard enough to justify doing anything beyond button-mashing, & I don’t really know if the endgame modes have enough depth to make you learn combos instead of simply getting/upgrading better chars. Genshin was similar—it feigned combat depth by putting timers on everything & made you “learn combos” that would kill enemies faster. In reality, it just made you hug the enemy, press the same buttons but faster, & tested how much rng you were willing to put up with. Gacha: I might be dumb but the new server still has gacha—it’s just streamlined. You farm rift shards which let you pull for a char/weapon, & the one you get is random. The banners aren’t timed, but rift shards can still be *BOUGHT* with real money. This is literally gacha, & the only gacha they completely removed was for matrixes (genshin artifacts). Finally, they removed the daily feature where you could hide a device on the map for resources & other players could steal it. Not a big deal, but it was cute. Positives: ToF mastered *scale.* Every environment truly feels vast, like you *are* exploring an unknown world, but not so big that it’s overwhelming, & not too empty it’s underwhelming. This is a very hard thing to get right, & even though Genshin/WuWa/BotW does this very well, there are many times in these games where areas feel smaller than they should be (like Genshin relies a lot on the same lighting tricks to give the *illusion* of far-ness). But I have never experienced this in ToF, & everything feels *vast,* without your char feeling small/invisible. When you start approaching Mirroria, you can’t help but stop & marvel at how you *are* actually stepping into a giant, floating city that feels size-accurate to when you’re also in the city itself. I don’t doubt other regions look equally as amazing. Worldbuilding. I actually think the worldbuilding is the best out of any gacha. It has a lot of outer space nonsense, but doesn’t have so many roaming parts that it becomes hard to follow (like HSR). It deals with a post-apocalyptic world, but the world does not look bleak or dreary. It’s similar to BotW in that it’s bright & beautiful, which actually makes you want to explore rather than creep around in a dark, broken environment. There’s a sense of emptiness to it, like after the disaster, nature reclaimed what were once civilizations. Ppl still live worrying about radiation & lack of resources, but everyone did their best to makeshift and go on with their lives. There’s a sense of hope & renewal that most similar games don’t have. [b]TLDR; ToF excels at few & is bad at many. *I do not believe that powercreep was what killed the game,* since it started dying even before powercreep, & other games have bad powercreep & are still popular (like HSR, again). What is killing it is lack of polish & devs that don’t understand how small issues can break your game if they’re compounded. The warp server changes little & the issues that casual players feel the most are still there. Bc of this, ToF will continue to be unable to hook in new players.[/b]

After the so-called “migration” in ToF, the account situation became genuinely problematic. This was not a simple update or server transfer — it was effectively a publisher and infrastructure change, where old accounts were not automatically preserved. Players had to manually complete a data transfer process within a limited time window. Some managed to do it in time, but a significant portion of the player base simply lost access to their accounts: characters, progress, and purchases became unavailable with no real chance of recovery. At the same time, part of the users did not even receive clear notifications or proper instructions. As a result, instead of a unified system, there is a split between the “old” and “new” versions of the game, and instead of a transparent migration, there is data loss for some players and confusion with login systems. If the project is positioned as an MMO with long-term progression, such transitions should either be fully automatic or significantly more reliable. In its current state, it feels like a risky and poorly implemented system where responsibility for account preservation was effectively shifted onto the player.

Tower of Fantasy, developed by Hotta Studio and published by Perfect World Games, is an ambitious free-to-play open-world MMORPG that blends futuristic science fiction with anime-inspired visuals and large-scale online multiplayer gameplay. Set on the distant planet of Aida, the story revolves around humanity's attempt to escape Earth's decline and build a new civilization powered by the mysterious Omnium energy. What begins as a technological breakthrough soon leads to disaster, leaving the world scarred by catastrophe and filled with dangerous creatures, rival factions, and forgotten mysteries. This narrative creates an engaging backdrop for a massive adventure that emphasizes exploration, action, and social interaction. The game's greatest achievement is the sheer scale of its world. Aida is packed with varied environments that constantly reward curiosity, from dense forests and sandy deserts to towering futuristic cities and frozen mountain ranges. Every region is filled with hidden treasures, environmental puzzles, exploration challenges, and optional activities that encourage players to venture away from the main storyline. Traversal feels fluid thanks to climbing, gliding, jetpacks, vehicles, and other mobility tools that make crossing long distances enjoyable instead of tedious. The combination of natural beauty and advanced technology gives each location its own personality, making exploration one of the most satisfying aspects of the experience. Combat stands out by favoring speed and flexibility over traditional MMORPG mechanics. Instead of selecting a permanent character class, players equip multiple weapons that can be swapped instantly during combat. Each weapon possesses its own abilities, elemental attributes, and fighting style, allowing players to create personalized combinations suited for different encounters. Battles are fast-paced and visually exciting, with perfectly timed dodges triggering slow-motion opportunities that reward precision and quick reactions. Boss encounters demand careful positioning and coordination, while ordinary enemies rarely become repetitive because of the wide variety of weapon combinations available throughout the game. Character customization also receives considerable attention. Players begin by creating their own avatar using an extensive selection of appearance options, giving everyone the opportunity to build a unique identity within the online world. As progression continues, equipment upgrades, relics, weapon enhancements, and additional customization systems steadily expand combat possibilities. The game also introduces Simulacra, powerful weapon users whose personalities, stories, and visual designs add additional flavor to the world without limiting player freedom. This approach successfully balances player creativity with memorable characters that enrich the game's lore. The multiplayer component reinforces Tower of Fantasy's MMORPG identity. Players can join friends or strangers to complete cooperative dungeons, challenge enormous world bosses, participate in guild activities, and engage in competitive multiplayer modes. Shared exploration naturally encourages teamwork, as players often encounter one another while traveling through the world or responding to large-scale events. Seasonal updates, limited-time activities, and expanding regions help maintain long-term interest, ensuring that both new and veteran players regularly have fresh objectives to pursue. Visually, the game presents a colorful and highly stylized interpretation of science fiction. Anime-inspired character models, impressive visual effects, detailed environments, and futuristic architecture combine to create an appealing presentation that remains consistent throughout the adventure. The soundtrack complements each region effectively, shifting from peaceful orchestral themes during exploration to energetic compositions during combat. Smooth animations and flashy weapon skills further enhance the excitement of battles without sacrificing overall visual clarity. The narrative offers an interesting mix of science fiction, mystery, and survival. As players uncover the history of Omnium energy and the downfall of civilization on Aida, they gradually learn more about the world's factions, political struggles, and hidden secrets. While the storytelling occasionally progresses at an uneven pace, the setting itself remains compelling thanks to its rich lore and unique blend of futuristic technology and post-apocalyptic themes. The game succeeds in establishing an identity that differs from more traditional fantasy MMORPGs while providing enough world-building to encourage continued exploration. Like many modern free-to-play online games, Tower of Fantasy includes progression systems tied to premium currencies, collectible weapons, cosmetics, and ongoing live-service updates. Players can experience a substantial amount of content without making purchases, but acquiring specific premium weapons or maximizing endgame performance may require considerable time investment or optional spending. Those familiar with gacha mechanics will recognize these systems immediately, while others may find the monetization less appealing despite the generous amount of free content available. Overall, Tower of Fantasy successfully combines expansive open-world exploration, stylish real-time combat, deep customization, and large-scale multiplayer systems into a polished online adventure. Its impressive environments, satisfying weapon mechanics, and cooperative gameplay create a rewarding experience for players who enjoy persistent online worlds and continuous content updates. Although its live-service design and monetization may not appeal to everyone, the game delivers a rich science-fiction MMORPG filled with memorable locations, engaging action, and meaningful opportunities for exploration and teamwork. Rating: 7/10

So, I’m a new player, i play on PC, and honestly, my first impression of Tower of Fantasy was pretty good! I customised my character and she turned out SO cute.💕 I was really happy with her, and the character customisation is definitely one of the things I liked the most. I’m still a little confused about the gacha system and how exactly you’re supposed to get weapons/characters, though. I’m usually more into classic MMORPGs, so I’m not really used to this kind of system. The game also throws a LOT of information at you at the beginning, and I’ll admit… I was too lazy to read all of it. 😭 So some of my confusion is probably partly my fault. I also ran into some issues with the voice acting/audio. Some voice lines seemed to be missing, while others were suddenly in English even though I had set my voice language to Japanese. It was pretty weird and took me out of the experience a little. But the biggest problem I had was the story progression. The game really doesn't feel very beginner-friendly if you're trying to actually follow the story in order. I got what felt like a massive spoiler very early on, because at some point the game suddenly wanted to send me to Vera or something??? And suddenly I was seeing Shirli's new appearance and getting information that, as a completely new player, I definitely wasn't expecting to see yet. At first, I genuinely thought my game had bugged out or that I had somehow skipped a bunch of quests. But then I checked my quests because I’m familiar with classic MMORPGs and I thought, "Okay, maybe I should check what I'm actually supposed to be doing before I follow this new quest." And that's when I realised that the story I was actually supposed to be experiencing had basically been pushed aside and turned into a side/Memory quest, while the game was trying to move me forward into later content. And honestly… WHAT 😭 I understand that the game is trying to help players catch up with the newer content, and technically the older story isn't gone. I could manually go back and track the original quests. But as a new player, I shouldn't have to already know that. If I'm playing the game for the first time and the game tells me to follow the main quest, I'm obviously going to assume that the main quest is the story I'm supposed to be following. Instead, I suddenly found myself being pushed into later content and seeing characters and story developments that I hadn't properly reached yet. That's what bothered me the most. I even looked online afterwards because I genuinely thought this was just something weird happening to my game, but I found other new players talking about having the exact same confusion. So I don't think Tower of Fantasy is necessarily a bad game. I actually think there's a lot here that I could enjoy. The graphics are really pretty, the character customisation is adorable, and I'm sure the game becomes much easier to understand once you've played it for a while. But I do think the onboarding is really confusing for a completely new player. There's a lot of information thrown at you, the gacha system can be confusing if you're coming from a more traditional MMORPG background, and the way the story progression works can make it really easy to accidentally spoil yourself or think you've skipped something. And for me personally, that really killed my motivation to continue. I didn't finish the game because I stopped playing after that. I did try to continue the original story manually, but honestly, I was still disappointed that I had already been shown such a major development before I was supposed to experience it. So, as someone who is new to Tower of Fantasy, I wouldn't personally recommend it as a first MMORPG if you're someone who really cares about following the story naturally and understanding everything as you go. That doesn't mean I think the game is bad. It's more like… I think Tower of Fantasy can be enjoyable once you understand how everything works, but getting to that point as a new player can be unnecessarily confusing. 😭 Still, the graphics are beautiful, and the character customisation is genuinely SO good. 💕 That's probably the part I had the most fun with!
